messages.author: 986d3b6442837cf2
messages.subject: Indicator variable disappeared with RJ?
parts:
Hi all,

Firstly, I'm really excited about NIMBLE. It's been a while since I've played around with BUGS and I'm really diggin' the work you folks have done on NIMBLE. Great stuff.

I have what is a relatively simple model that includes an indicator for model selection. I followed the reversible jump example and everything seems to be working but when I try to extract the samples of the indicator they are completely gone.

Here's what I mean:

R> unique(sub('\\[[0-9]+\\]', '', colnames(samples_rj)))
[1] "dispersion" "psi"        "shift"      "t_lower"    "t_upper"

'shift' has an indicator going into it (z) which is not appearing in the samples. psi is the prior on z which actually does appear in the samples.

here's how I configured the RJ sampler:

configureRJ(conf = full_configuration,
  targetNodes = c('shift'),
  indicatorNodes = c('z'),
  control = list(mean = 0, scale = 1)
  )

And here is the actual model:

full_code = nimbleCode({
  dispersion ~ dexp(1 / 200)
  for (n in 1:N) {
    t_lower[n] ~ dnorm(-1.04, sd = 1)
    t_upper[n] ~ dnorm(1.04, sd = 1)
    constraint[n] ~ dconstraint(t_lower[n] < t_upper[n])
  }

  psi ~ dbeta(1, 1)
  for (g in 1:G) {
    z[g] ~ dbern(psi)
    # z[g] <- zi[g] * (1 - nt_control[g])
    shift[g] ~ dnorm(0, sd = 100)
    for (n in 1:N) {
      q[n, g, 1] <- phi(t_lower[n] - z[g] * shift[g])
      q[n, g, 3] <- 1 - phi(t_upper[n] - z[g] * shift[g])
      q[n, g, 2] <- 1 - q[n, g, 3] - q[n, g, 1]
      alpha[n, g, 1:3] <- dispersion * q[n, g, 1:3]

      x[n, g, 1:3] ~ ddirchmulti(alpha[n, g, 1:3], x_total[n, g])
    }
  }
})


Would appreciate any feedback you might have.

Thanks in advance!


Best,

Harold

messages.author: ac2eba1e47ae807d
messages.subject: Re: Indicator variable disappeared with RJ?
parts:
Hi Harold,

Happy to hear you are trying out NIMBLE and the reversible jump!

About your problem, is the indicator variable z in the monitors? 

Only variables that are monitored will have their samples saved for use outside of the MCMC. From your example, you can check which variables are monitored via   full_configuration$monitors() and in case add the indicator variables via full_configuration$addMonitors('z').

The default MCMC configuration includes monitors on all top-level stochastic nodes of the model, and I think that the indicator variables would not be included by default. 

Let me know if this works!

Best, 

Sally
